data.title: Tencent Cloud Sales Rise 35% as Adjusted Operating Profit Falls
data.description:
Tencent (HKEX: 0700) said on November 18 that cloud services revenue grew 35% from a year earlier in the third quarter. Demand for AI services helped drive that growth, while the cost of expanding computing capacity strained cash flow and adjusted operating profit fell.

Total revenue reached RMB207.3 billion in the three months ended September 30, up 8% from a year earlier and below the RMB210.77 billion LSEG estimate, Reuters reported. Revenue growth slowed from 11% in the second quarter. Domestic game revenue grew 11%, while international game revenue fell 9% against a stronger year-earlier comparison.

Adjusted operating profit fell 6% to RMB68.1 billion, and the corresponding margin fell to 33% from 38%, according to Tencent’s earnings release. On an IFRS basis, operating profit fell 7% to RMB59.1 billion. Profit attributable to shareholders rose 0.8% to RMB63.6 billion, according to the exchange filing.

Capital expenditure payments more than tripled to RMB65.1 billion from a year earlier. The company reported negative free cash flow of RMB69.1 billion and said the figure would have been positive RMB16.9 billion excluding prepayments for computing capacity. Tencent said those advance payments support both its own AI products and demand from cloud customers.

data.title: Target Sales Rise 7.1% as Retailer Lifts Full-Year Outlook
data.description:
Target (NYSE: TGT) reported $27.1 billion in third-quarter net sales on November 18, up 7.1% from a year earlier. The retailer raised its annual sales outlook heading into the holidays as established stores and online sales both grew.

Comparable sales rose 5.6% in the quarter ended October 31. Comparable store sales increased 4.6% and comparable digital sales rose 9.8%, according to Target’s earnings release. The company said sales so far in November were running in line with its outlook, at a faster pace than in October.

Both GAAP and adjusted diluted earnings were $2.65 a share, including 50 cents from tariff refunds. Target recognized $301 million of refunds before tax in the quarter. Excluding that benefit, adjusted earnings would have been $2.15 a share, 21% above $1.78 a year earlier. Gross margin rose to 30.5%, with 1.1 percentage points of the gain coming from refunds.

Target now projects about 6% net sales growth for fiscal 2026, up from about 5% after its second-quarter report. The range for GAAP and adjusted earnings rose to $10.65–$11.40 a share from $9.90–$10.90, the Associated Press reported. The new range includes $2.14 a share in refunds already recognized and excludes any future refunds.

The retailer expects to spend $5 billion to $6 billion on capital projects in 2027. In the nearer term, it is competing for holiday shoppers after cutting prices on nearly 2,000 additional items during the third quarter, according to the AP.

data.title: UK Inflation Rises to 3.6% as Fuel Prices Jump
data.description:
UK consumer prices rose 3.6% from a year earlier in October, up from 3.5% in September and the highest rate in a year, the Office for National Statistics said on November 18. Fuel drove much of the increase, while core and services inflation held steady. The report comes after the Bank of England raised interest rates earlier this month.

Motor fuel prices rose 33.2% from a year earlier, up from 29.8% in September. Diesel averaged 199.5 pence a litre in October, the highest price in the ONS series dating back to January 1996. Across the full consumer basket, prices rose 0.5% from September.

Core inflation, which excludes energy, food, alcohol and tobacco, stayed at 2.8%. Services inflation was unchanged at 3.7%, while goods inflation rose to 3.5% from 3.2%. The split matters to policymakers looking for signs that higher energy costs are spreading to other prices.

The Bank of England raised its benchmark rate to 4% from 3.75% on November 5. Its next decision is due December 17. October’s headline figure matched the median estimate in a Reuters poll and came in below the bank’s 3.7% forecast. Services inflation also came in below the poll’s 3.8% forecast. Reuters reported on Wednesday morning that traders pared bets on a December increase after the release.

The bank projects inflation near 5% by mid-2027 as higher energy costs feed through to household bills. Its November minutes said evidence of those costs spreading to wages and other prices had been limited so far.

data.title: What’s Ahead for the Stock Market This Week
data.description:
After Friday’s sharp selloff triggered by President Trump’s decision to raise tariffs in response to China tightening rare earth exports, investors are starting the week on edge. The focus now shifts to trade tensions, earnings season, and the Federal Reserve’s next moves.

Big Earnings Week: Banks and Chipmakers Take Center Stage

This week kicks off a busy stretch of third-quarter results from major financial firms and tech companies.

  • Banks: JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, and Citigroup all report on Tuesday, followed by Bank of America and Morgan Stanley on Wednesday. Later in the week, American Express, Truist Financial, and State Street will wrap up the financial lineup.
  • Tech & Chips: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSMC) reports Thursday after strong AI chip sales boosted its revenue 40% in the first half of 2025. ASML follows on Wednesday after raising concerns about tariffs and slowing demand for chip equipment.
  • Tech events: Oracle’s AI World conference begins Monday, and Salesforce’s Dreamforce starts Tuesday — both likely to bring attention to artificial intelligence and enterprise tech. Earnings Calendar >>

Data Delays and Fed Watch

The federal government shutdown, now entering its third week, is likely to delay several key reports, including retail sales, inflation (PPI), housing starts, and jobless claims. Some data will still come through, like the NFIB Small Business Optimism Index on Tuesday and homebuilder confidence on Thursday.

Investors will also tune in to Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell’s speech on Tuesday, along with comments from Fed officials, including Michelle Bowman and Christopher Waller. The Fed’s Beige Book, which gives an overview of economic conditions across regions, will be released on Wednesday.

Market Context

Bond markets will be closed on Monday for Columbus Day (also observed as Indigenous Peoples Day), but stock exchanges will remain open.

With limited economic data and uncertainty around Washington’s budget standoff, markets are likely to take their cues from corporate earnings and Fed commentary.

In short, this week is about navigating through noise — balancing worries over tariffs and the shutdown against potential optimism from strong bank and chipmaker earnings.

data.title: What Is the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA)? A Complete Guide
data.description:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA), often referred to as the Dow Jones, the Dow 30, or simply the Dow, is one of the world’s most recognized stock market indexes. The DJIA tracks 30 of the largest publicly traded companies in the United States, making it a widely followed indicator of the overall health of the U.S. economy and stock market. Investors searching for DJIA today, DJIA futures, or Dow Jones price updates often turn to this index as a barometer of market sentiment.

But what exactly is the DJIA, what stocks does it include, and how do traders and long-term investors use it in their strategies?

What Is the DJIA?

The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) is a price-weighted index created in 1896 by Charles Dow and Edward Jones. Unlike market-cap-weighted indexes like the S&P 500, the DJIA assigns weight based on a stock’s price rather than its market capitalization. This means a company with a higher stock price (e.g., Apple or UnitedHealth) influences the index more heavily than lower-priced stocks.

The DJIA is designed to reflect the performance of blue-chip companies across different sectors of the U.S. economy. It does not include utilities or transportation stocks, which are tracked by separate Dow indexes.

What Companies Are in the DJIA?

The DJIA is composed of 30 large, publicly traded U.S. companies that are considered leaders in their industries. These companies span sectors such as technology, finance, healthcare, consumer goods, and industrials.

Here’s a snapshot of the DJIA holdings (as of 2025, September 15th):

Note: The index is reviewed periodically, and constituents may change depending on mergers, bankruptcies, or shifts in market relevance.

How Does the DJIA Work?

  • Price-Weighted Methodology: Higher-priced stocks have more influence.
  • Dow Divisor: A proprietary number adjusted for stock splits, dividends, and corporate actions ensures continuity.
  • Sector Balance: While tech stocks (Apple, Microsoft) now hold significant weight, the index aims to represent the broader U.S. economy.

If Apple (AAPL) rises $5 in a day, it has the same impact on the DJIA as Boeing (BA) rising $5, even though their market caps differ drastically.

Why Do Investors Watch the DJIA?

  • Economic Barometer: The DJIA today is seen as a snapshot of the U.S. economy.
  • Historical Importance: Created in 1896, it has over 125 years of market history.
  • Market Sentiment: Widely quoted on news outlets and financial platforms.
  • Trading Opportunities: Investors follow DJIA futures, DJIA ETFs, and Dow Jones index funds for exposure.

How to Trade or Invest in the DJIA

Investors can’t buy the DJIA directly but can gain exposure through exchange-traded funds (ETFs), futures contracts, or mutual funds:

  • SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (DIA) – tracks the DJIA closely.
  • DJIA Futures – contracts traded on CME, allowing leveraged exposure.
  • Index Funds – designed for long-term buy-and-hold investors.

data.title: Stock Futures Rebound After Nvidia Beat as Fed Minutes Loom
data.description:
U.S. stock futures rebounded before the opening bell on Wednesday, November 18, after Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) beat earnings expectations. The recovery follows the S&P 500’s fourth straight loss and a sharp software selloff. The next test comes from the Federal Reserve’s October meeting minutes, with markets already assigning a high probability to another rate increase in December.

In CNBC’s update at 4:45 a.m. ET Wednesday, Nasdaq-100 futures were up 1%, S&P 500 futures gained 0.58% and Dow futures rose 0.32%. Nvidia shares were almost 3% higher in premarket trading. These are early-session indications, rather than gains in the regular cash session. In today’s pre-market video briefing, we examine the same tension between renewed demand for AI infrastructure stocks and pressure on software businesses.

At Tuesday’s November 17 regular-session close, the S&P 500 stood at 7,340.53, down 1.03% and at its lowest close since late July. The Nasdaq Composite fell 0.74% to 24,328.38. The Dow lost 848.75 points, or 1.64%, to 50,759.42 after falling more than 1,000 points at its session low, according to CNBC’s closing report. Wednesday’s futures bounce therefore comes after substantial losses, rather than from an undisturbed market.

Software was a particular weak spot. Salesforce (NYSE: CRM) closed Tuesday at $194.52, down 9.45%; Yahoo Finance’s historical prices show a previous close of $214.83. Yahoo’s software coverage described concerns that AI agents could reduce demand for traditional software subscriptions. The selling came a day before Anthropic’s expected IPO pricing. That timing does not establish that the offering caused the decline.

Nvidia’s fiscal third-quarter release supplied the overnight counterweight: revenue rose 103% from a year earlier to $115.8 billion, and its fourth-quarter sales forecast was $130 billion, plus or minus 3%. The margin outlook was lower, however. Our separate Nvidia results report covers those figures in detail. The broader question for Wednesday is whether the positive earnings response spreads beyond the infrastructure trade.

The Fed’s calendar schedules minutes of the October 27–28 meeting for 2 p.m. ET today. The October statement recorded a 10–2 vote to hold rates at 3.75%–4%, with Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack preferring a quarter-point increase. In its November 18 morning report, Trading Economics cited CME FedWatch pricing of nearly 96% for a quarter-point December hike. That is a market-implied probability, not a Fed commitment; the December meeting is scheduled for December 8–9.

Oil offers another part of the backdrop. Reuters reported that API figures showed U.S. crude inventories increased by 5.28 million barrels in the week ended November 13. The report also described Iranian drone attacks on a U.S. radar system in Bahrain and U.S. strikes on a missile launch site on Qeshm Island. The inventory increase and continuing supply risks point in opposing directions for oil.

Before the open, Target (NYSE: TGT), Lowe’s (NYSE: LOW) and TJX (NYSE: TJX) are scheduled to report, while October housing starts and permits are due today, according to the Census release schedule. Anthropic is expected to price its IPO tonight ahead of a planned Thursday Nasdaq debut. CNBC’s offering report gives a proposed $70–$78 range; its latest market coverage says sources expect pricing above that range. The final offer price has not yet been set.

data.title: Japan’s Exports Rise 20.5% to a Record as Higher Imports Widen Deficit
data.description:
Japan’s goods exports rose 20.5% from a year earlier to a record ¥11.77 trillion in October. Imports grew faster, leaving a ¥476.5 billion trade deficit, according to provisional figures the Ministry of Finance released on November 18.

The trade tables show shipments to the United States increased 23.9% by value, while exports to China rose 13.3%. The ministry’s breakdown shows that exports of semiconductor manufacturing equipment climbed 49.7% and automobile exports rose 19.9%. Those categories give investors a more specific picture of where export receipts grew.

The export volume index increased 5.8% from a year earlier, well below the headline increase in yen terms. The import volume index fell 0.2% even as the import bill rose 21.6% to ¥12.25 trillion. Crude oil imports were up 60.5% by value, making energy one of the biggest contributors to the higher bill.

The deficit widened from ¥301.9 billion in October 2025. It was smaller than the ¥956 billion shortfall economists had expected, Reuters reported. Chip-related demand supported exports, while higher energy costs pushed up the value of imports.

The October figures add a first look at goods trade after the period covered in Japan’s July–September GDP report. The gap between export value and volume growth is worth following when assessing how much stronger overseas sales translate into higher production.

data.title: Nvidia Revenue Doubles to $115.8 Billion, With $130 Billion Q4 Outlook
data.description:
Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) reported $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue on November 17, more than double the year-earlier figure. In its first earnings report under interim CEO Colette Kress, the chipmaker forecast $130 billion in revenue for the following quarter, plus or minus 3%.

Revenue for the fiscal third quarter ended October 25 rose 103% from a year earlier and 20% from the preceding quarter, according to Nvidia’s earnings release. Data Center sales reached $107.6 billion, up 110% year over year and accounting for about 93% of company revenue. Nvidia reported diluted earnings of $2.70 a share under GAAP and $2.68 on an adjusted basis.

The midpoint of the fourth-quarter sales forecast exceeded the $125.25 billion average estimate compiled by LSEG, Reuters reported. The fiscal fourth quarter includes an extra week, which matters when comparing sales with the preceding quarter. Nvidia’s forecast assumes zero Data Center compute revenue from China.

Nvidia expects adjusted gross margin of 71% to 72% in the fourth quarter, down from 74.9% in the third. The company also said it began shipping its Vera Rubin NVL72 systems during the reported quarter. The sales and margin forecasts point to a quarter with more revenue and less gross profit per dollar of sales.

The results follow the board’s creation of an export-control oversight committee. For the operating outlook, the figures to watch are the pace of data center shipments and whether Nvidia delivers the higher sales implied by its guidance at the lower margin it projects.

data.title: Elbit Reports $33 Billion Backlog as Quarterly Revenue Grows 17%
data.description:
Elbit Systems (NASDAQ: ESLT) reported a record $33 billion order backlog alongside 17% revenue growth in its November 17 third-quarter results. The defense technology company said Europe was the main source of the backlog increase during the quarter.

For the three months ended September 30, revenue reached $2.252 billion, compared with $1.922 billion a year earlier. GAAP net income attributable to shareholders increased to $177.9 million from $133.4 million, while diluted earnings rose to $3.70 per share from $2.80. S&P Capital IQ’s results report corroborated those sales and earnings comparisons.

The company’s release separately reported non-GAAP diluted earnings of $4.36 per share, up from $3.35. Those adjusted figures should be distinguished from the reported GAAP result when assessing the quarter.

Approximately 74% of the backlog came from orders outside Israel. About 35% was scheduled for performance during the remainder of 2026 and 2027. This is contracted future work, rather than quarterly revenue already recognized.

Management expects high-teens revenue growth and continued margin expansion in 2027 compared with full-year 2026. That is a forward-looking estimate; the sales, earnings and backlog figures describe the reported quarter and September 30 position.

data.title: Klarna Revenue Rises 12% as Credit-Loss Provision Rate Falls
data.description:
Klarna Group (NYSE: KLAR) reported 12% revenue growth for the third quarter of 2026, alongside a lower credit-loss provision rate and a narrower net loss. The November 17 results show improving transaction economics as payment volume continued to expand.

Revenue reached $1.009 billion, while gross merchandise value increased 10% to $36.1 billion, according to Klarna’s release. U.S. merchandise volume grew 24%, faster than the group’s overall rate. Investing.com’s results coverage corroborated those growth figures and the company’s fourth consecutive quarter above $1 billion in revenue.

Transaction margin dollars rose 32% to $371 million. Klarna defines that measure as revenue remaining after processing, credit and funding costs. It therefore describes transaction economics, rather than the company’s final net profit.

Adjusted operating income was $21 million, an improvement of $35 million from a year earlier. The group nevertheless recorded a $65 million net loss, although that loss narrowed by $30 million. A positive adjusted operating result and a net loss are different measures of the same quarter.

Provisions for credit losses declined to 0.56% of merchandise volume from 0.72% a year earlier. Klarna attributed the improvement to underwriting and a larger share of loans being offloaded. Active consumers reached 122 million, up 7%. The report pairs network growth with better transaction margins, while the net result shows the business has not yet turned that progress into overall profitability.
